description:
ol-style-name-case (issue #854): a built-in name's IDENTITY is profile-independent while its AVAILABILITY is not, pinned in one fixture. `challenge` is the Tutor profile's primitive (spec/conformance.md:244) and only `core-language` is active here, so `ol-unknown-command` is the correct, conforming answer to "can this run?" (spec/tooling.md:175-177 — the checker MUST use the active profile set to decide which primitives are available). The casing warning beside it answers the different question spec/tooling.md:243 asks — "built-ins should be shown lowercase" — which spec/grammar.md:412 makes profile-independent, because "a program cannot declare which profiles it requires" and "what a profile decides is whether a name *works*, never whether a program may declare it".

The two findings carry DIFFERENT params by design (issue #1005): `ol-unknown-command` reports the case-folded resolution identity `challenge` (every casing of one absent callable is one condition, one identity — spec/error-model.md:255-260), while `ol-style-name-case` reports the source spelling `CHALLENGE` because the offending casing IS the subject it flags.

This fixture also records an ABSORPTION. When #854 derived this lint from the registries, `challenge` was the one built-in name with no registry at all and was documented as unreachable. #838 then registered TUTOR_PRIMITIVE_ARITY in PROFILE_PRIMITIVE_ARITY_TABLES, and the casing coverage appeared with NO change to checker-style.ts — which is the property epic #900 is asking for, and the one a hand-written name list cannot have.
